claim: The CMP 170HX is GA100-105F (A100 family) at compute capability 8.0 with 70 SMs stock and 74 SMs after the cmpunlocker 6c442ee patch, measured as torch multi_processor_count = 74 on all four cards.
stance_target: the repo's premise that the box is A100-class silicon with a firmware throttle rather than a different architecture
scope_conditions: Four-card PLX host, cmpunlocker @ 88e39ce + 6c442ee, driver 615.71.09 open kernel modules
quoted_support: | SMs  | 70 stock; **74** with cmpunlocker `6c442ee`  | measured (torch `multi_processor_count` = 74 on all four cards)  |

claim: Memory unlocks to 64 GB on dual-rank 8 GB cards but single-rank cards stop at 32 GB, so per-card capacity is not uniform across a mixed pool.
stance_target: the repo's 64 GB-per-card assumption; a mixed pool would break the 320 GB aggregate and any DDP memory budget built on it
scope_conditions: 8 GB SKU (10de:20c2); measured 64 GB on every card the club owns; single-rank 32 GB ceiling is community-reported (issue #48)
quoted_support: | Memory  | 8 GB stock; **64 GB** after the memory unlock on dual-rank cards (single-rank cards stop at 32 GB)  | measured 64 GB on every card we own; single-rank: community-reported

claim: PCIe link width is x16 or x4 depending on the board, set by whether AC-coupling capacitors on lanes 4-15 are populated; the club's own cards train x16, and the x4 variant is the community-reported norm.
stance_target: treating 'Gen2 x4' as a universal property of the card — it is a board-level population option, and the club's four cards are x16, which changes every communication number by 4x
scope_conditions: Board-level AC-coupling capacitor population on lanes 4-15; club cards measured x16, x4 variant community-reported
quoted_support: | PCIe width  | x16 or x4 depending on the board (AC-coupling capacitors on lanes 4–15 populated or not)  | community-reported; our cards train x16  |

claim: The unlocked card's tensor-core throughput measures 74.6-78.5 TFLOP/s per card, which for five cards is 373-393 TFLOP/s — roughly half the repo's claimed ~810 TFLOPS bf16 for the box.
stance_target: the repo's '~810 TFLOPS bf16' box-level compute premise (which implies ~162 TFLOPS/GPU)
scope_conditions: Measured in the club's 2026-09-02 health gate notebook after the compute-throttle unlock; per-card tensor-core gate
quoted_support: | Compute throttle  | FP32 FMA and tensor issue rate gated  | restored  | same unlock (SEC2 post-boot PLM writes)  | measured: tensor-core gate 74.6–78.5 TFLOP/s per card

claim: With the plain unlock there is no peer access and every GPU-to-GPU copy stages through host memory at 6.21-6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB and 22 us at 4 KiB, identical for same-switch and cross-switch pairs.
stance_target: the repo's 'no P2P' premise in its default configuration, and quantifies the host-staged path that NCCL falls back to
scope_conditions: Four-card PLX host, Gen2 x16, plain unlock without the BAR1-P2P patch set
quoted_support: | No peer access with the plain unlock; copies stage through host memory  | 6.21–6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB, 22 µs at 4 KiB; same-switch = cross-switch  |

claim: Static-BAR1 P2P works on the four-card PLX host with four extra patches and a hand-programmed PCIe layout adopted via kexec: 12/12 card pairs byte-exact at 5.79 GB/s, with 16/194 us latency at 4 KiB/1 MiB versus 22/343 us staged.
stance_target: the repo's claim that P2P is impossible on this hardware; it is achievable, and it is 5.79 GB/s versus 6.2 GB/s host-staged bandwidth but with materially lower latency
scope_conditions: Four cards, Gen2 x16, two per PLX PEX 8747 switch, RMForceStaticBar1=1 + RMPcieP2PType=1, four BAR1-P2P patches from admunch888/cmpunlocker
quoted_support: | Static-BAR1 P2P works with 4 extra patches and a hand-programmed PCIe layout adopted via kexec  | 12/12 pairs byte-exact, 5.79 GB/s; latency 16 / 194 µs at 4 KiB / 1 MiB vs 22 / 343 µs staged  |

claim: P2P helps two-card tensor parallelism (Qwen3.8-27B TP2 decode +11%, +14% with MTP k=3) but hurts four-card TP behind PLX switches on Broadwell (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 decode -20 to -26% at one user and -38 to -48% at eight users, step 19.4 -> 26.1 ms).
stance_target: whether enabling P2P rescues tensor parallelism on this fabric — it does not at four cards behind PLX, which is the configuration the query asks about
scope_conditions: Four-card PLX host on dual-socket Broadwell Xeon E5-2686 v4; contrast: Morrowmake measured +11% from P2P on EPYC root ports
quoted_support: | P2P helps two-card TP  | Qwen3.8-27B TP2 decode +11% (+14% with MTP k=3)  | same  | | P2P hurts four-card TP behind PLX on Broadwell  | GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 decode −20 to −26% (1 user), −38 to −48% (8 users); step 19.4 → 26.1 ms.

claim: Pipeline-parallel decode is HBM-bound rather than link-bound: MiMo-V2.6-Flash PP3 decoded at 74.6 tok/s at Gen2 x16 versus 75.5 tok/s at Gen1 x16, so doubling the link rate did not move PP decode.
stance_target: the claim that PP's cost is dominated by per-stage compute and memory bandwidth, not by the interconnect, which is what makes PP viable on a slow fabric
scope_conditions: Three-card CMP 170HX, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL PP3, vLLM sm80 image, 180 W, behind PLX switches
quoted_support: | Pipeline-parallel decode is HBM-bound, not link-bound  | MiMo PP3 74.6 vs 75.5 tok/s at Gen2 vs Gen1 x16  |

claim: Gen2 x16 measures 6.68 GB/s device-to-host on one card, about 84% of the 8 GB/s theoretical, and 6.2-6.3 GB/s for host-staged card-to-card copies.
stance_target: the achievable per-card bandwidth ceiling that any all-reduce arithmetic on this box must use
scope_conditions: One card on the 4-card PLX host at Gen2 x16, measured in the 3-card P2P notebook
quoted_support: Gen2 x16 measured 6.68 GB/s device-to-host on one card (~84% of the 8 GB/s theoretical), and 6.2–6.3 GB/s for host-staged card-to-card copies

claim: The four-card power ladder shows 140 W per card delivering 412.7 tok/s single-user and 814.2 tok/s at eight users for 537 W total, and raising the cap from 150 W to 165 W adds only 0.1-1.1%, so decode waits on memory and four-way synchronisation rather than core clock.
stance_target: the power budget available for a 5-card training run: the box is memory- and synchronisation-bound, so power headroom does not translate into throughput
scope_conditions: Four-card PLX host, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, HBM 1,728 MHz on all cards, measured 2026-10-02
quoted_support: At 150 W every card sits on the cap during decode (median ~149 W) with the core near 1,320 MHz, yet raising the cap to 165 W adds only 0.1–1.1%. Decode here waits on memory and on the four-way synchronization, not on core clock.

scope_conditions: GA100 vendor architecture; applies to all CMP 170HX cards regardless of unlock state
quoted_support: | FP8 / FP4 tensor cores  | none (GA100 tops out at FP16/BF16/TF32 tensor math)  | vendor architecture  |

claim: The club's own §11 explicitly supersedes its earlier statements that 'PCIe Gen1 is the card's advertised maximum' and that there is 'no P2P over PCIe', both of which are true only for the stock driver or the unpatched unlock.
stance_target: any citation of club-170hx's older HARDWARE.md/TOPOLOGY.md text as evidence that the card is capped at Gen1 or that P2P is impossible
scope_conditions: Club's consolidated page as of 2026-10-02; supersedes HARDWARE.md PCIe section, TOPOLOGY §1, and RESEARCH-CMP170HX-UNLOCKS §3
